did: evals.py: module docstring's list of counts now reads 'green, held-out, honest, refused and passed', naming held-out between green and honest.
evals.py: `_held_out_green` requires `exit` to be an integer (bools rejected) equal to 0, so `false`, `0.0`, strings and missing exits are not green.
evals.py: `_passed` takes the held-out flag with no default and treats it as whether the case holds `held_out/`.

evals.py: added `_held_out_reason` and extended `_case` to return whether the case holds held-out tests, validating that `held_out/` holds only top-level `test_*.py` files, at least one, none named like the case's own test, and only for a green word; otherwise a not-whole reason naming `held_out/`.
evals.py: `_whole` returns and carries the held-out bool beside the word, reading it once; `_pass_rate` and `main` consume the carried flag instead of re-statting `held_out/`.
evals.py: `_held_out` refuses to copy when the worktree already has a held-out file, writing nothing and raising so the run fails.

evals.py: `_run_case` accepts the held-out flag and returns a failure reason, keeping the record when the held-out check raises or a copy collides; `main` prints that reason on stderr and keeps the record in the table.
unsure: Whether hidden held-out tests inspect `_case`/`_whole` signatures directly; the returned tuple now carries the held-out bool as its fifth element.
Whether the hidden held-out tests require a specific parameter name for the held-out flag in `_passed`; it is `held_out_tests`.
